r0_observed: PR #557 temporarily calls Connection.enable_load_extension(True), loads the hash-bound guard extension, then disables extension loading.
Python documents that check_same_thread=False permits one sqlite3.Connection to be accessed from multiple threads, with user serialization obligations.

SQLite documents that sqlite3_enable_load_extension enables both the C load API and the SQL load_extension() function and recommends SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION when only the C API is needed.
grf.hypothesis: The candidate's temporary extension-loading enablement is effectively private to load_guard and cannot be observed by another user of the same shared connection.
grf.strongest_counterhypothesis: If the same connection is thread-shared and execution interleaves after enablement but before disablement, another holder of that connection can use the temporary load capability.
grf.falsifier: One disposable shared sqlite3.Connection with check_same_thread=False; intentionally force one scheduler yield immediately after enable_load_extension(True), then have a second thread attempt to load a benign marker extension before the guard path disables extension loading.
collapse: REJECT general inference: temporary enable_load_extension(True) is connection-private or intrinsically race-free.
RETAIN the hash/open-fd binding of the intended guard artifact as useful for that intended load only.
DEFER production exploitability: the experiment deliberately forced an interleaving and did not run on accepted Hostinger or Frank ProductStart.

PROMOTION OBLIGATION: productive integration must either make guard loading a provably exclusive pre-publication/bootstrap operation, or use a stronger non-shared/non-loadable mechanism; SQL-level extension loading should remain disabled.

unusual_experiment.scope: disposable local temporary directory; benign diagnostic extensions only
unusual_experiment.intervention: A sqlite3.Connection subclass intentionally yielded after enabling extension loading. A second thread sharing that same connection attempted one benign marker-extension load during the enabled interval.
limitations: The scheduling yield was deliberately injected; natural exploit frequency was not measured.
The competing thread had direct Python Connection access, which is a stronger capability than SQL-only ingress.
No accepted-host, ProductStart, UnifiedDB or effect-authority mutation was performed.

primary_external_evidence.claim: check_same_thread=False permits multi-thread access to a connection and requires user serialization where needed.

primary_external_evidence.source: SQLite Enable Or Disable Extension Loading
primary_external_evidence.claim: sqlite3_enable_load_extension enables both C and SQL loading; SQLite recommends SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION to keep SQL load_extension disabled.
SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION enables the C sqlite3_load_extension interface independently of the SQL load_extension function.

recommended_hardening: Do not treat temporary Connection.enable_load_extension(True) as a safe production primitive on a connection that can already be shared or reached by competing execution.
At minimum keep SQL load_extension disabled via SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION when dynamic loading is unavoidable.

Require machine-checkable exclusive bootstrap/pre-publication ownership for the productive connection during any C-API extension load, or replace loadable diagnostics with a stronger built-in/static mechanism.
Add an ordinary regression/precondition that distinguishes exclusive bootstrap from a shared-connection state; do not claim this receipt closes the accepted Hostinger gate.
